capabilities.legal_transition: a new version for a strategy_id that already has registered StrategySpec entries must be either an idempotent replay of an existing (strategy_id, version) at the *same* registry_id, a legitimate immediate-next semver bump (major+1.0.0, major.minor+1.0, or major.minor.patch+1) from the current latest known version, or declare lineage.parent_registry_ids naming an existing StrategySpec entry for that strategy_id AND be a strictly greater version than that parent's (no downgrade); an arbitrary/out-of-sequence version, a downgrade below a linked parent's version, or a *different* registry_id claiming an already-registered (strategy_id, version, artifact_type) is rejected (400/409). The (strategy_id, version, artifact_type) tuple is enforced as a real atomic unique identity at the store layer (register_if_absent's unique_fields, backed by PostgresJsonOwnerStore.insert_if_absent's table lock / RegistryStore's single process lock) — two different caller-supplied registry_ids racing the same tuple commit exactly one winner.

bff_adapter_semantics.prior_defect: StrategyCommandAdapter._execute_strategy_action fabricated a resulting_status from a static action->status map and returned an authoritative_readback with zero owner I/O — architecture-resumption-sa-sd.md §2. A later fix added real owner I/O but still (a) silently replaced the caller's expected_metadata CAS precondition with a freshly-fetched GET, defeating CAS, (b) discarded the real PATCH response in favor of a second, independent GET that could return stale/unrelated/empty data and still be reported as success, (c) never validated that the caller-supplied registry_id actually belonged to the requested strategy_id (a cross-strategy write could be reported as success for the wrong aggregate), (d) mislabeled a bare updated_at timestamp as "version" in the receipt, and (e) compared a genuine idempotent replay's PATCH response against an independent "current" owner GET, which spuriously failed (READBACK_MISMATCH) whenever a later, unrelated command had since moved the row on.
bff_adapter_semantics.fix: update_params now requires and forwards the caller's own expected_metadata unchanged (no silent refresh-to-latest), performs a single real HTTP PATCH against the Registry metadata-CAS route, and builds its receipt from that PATCH response's entry snapshot plus its X-Idempotent-Replay header. A non-replay response is verified against a genuine owner GET readback (never trusted alone); a replay is trusted directly without a second GET, since it is itself the historically-committed snapshot. Both the PATCH response and any readback are checked against the requested strategy_id, failing closed with STRATEGY_ID_MISMATCH on a cross-aggregate registry_id. The receipt's "version" field now reports the entry's actual semver version, not updated_at. A readback failure immediately after a *confirmed* commit (the PATCH itself returned a concrete entry) is now reported as ActionUnavailableError(READBACK_UNAVAILABLE, retryable=True, downstream_status=503) rather than the flat non-retryable 422 used for a genuinely unsupported action — see command_executor.execute_command_with_status, which now propagates ActionUnavailableError.retryable/downstream_status instead of hardcoding them. submit_review/promote_paper/activate/pause/archive still raise ActionUnavailableError naming the exact owner from command_contract.py.
bff_adapter_semantics.unrelated_scope_preserved: RankingFormula and Ranking action handling in the same adapter file is untouched by this task; their pre-existing fake-receipt pattern is not claimed solved here.

tenant_scoped_aggregate_reads.note: GET /api/registry/strategies/{strategy_id}/latest-approved and GET /api/registry/strategies/{strategy_id}/deployment-view previously authenticated the caller but resolved the semver-latest approved entry across *all* tenants, so a caller in tenant B could receive tenant A's approved entry/deployment stage for a shared strategy_id. RegistryService.resolve_latest_approved/resolve_deployment_view (split_api.py) now accept an optional `visible` entry predicate; the two routes pass `_can_read_entry(ctx, entry)` so resolution itself is scoped to entries the caller's verified tenant (or an admin role, or a builtin) may see. The same `_can_read_entry` scoping was applied to the existing-versions lookup POST /api/registry/strategy-specs uses to decide the next legal semver (_validate_strategy_spec_version_lineage), which previously computed 'the latest known version' across all tenants for the same strategy_id.

generic_route_typed_content_validation.note: POST /api/registry/entries stored a caller-supplied checksum verbatim with no content validation. A bare artifact_type=strategy_spec reference entry (checksum only, no embedded content) is unaffected, but if a caller embeds an inline strategy_spec payload under metadata.strategy_spec through this generic path, it is now schema-validated (services/control-plane/specs/strategy_spec.schema.json) and its checksum is verified against the embedded content — mirroring the dedicated POST /api/registry/strategy-specs facade, which now also runs the same schema validator on every inline strategy_spec (previously it hashed the payload with no schema check at all — POST strategy_spec={} returned 200).

atomic_composite_identity_on_plain_creat.note: register() (the non-register_if_absent create path used by e.g. model_artifact entries and name-only drafts) previously inserted unconditionally with no composite-identity reservation at the store layer at all — only a non-atomic, best-effort application-layer check. RegistryStore.create/PostgresRegistryStore.create now accept unique_fields and atomically reserve (strategy_id, version, artifact_type) the same way register_if_absent does; a genuine collision under this path raises RegistryUniqueViolationError -> RegistryConflictError (409) instead of relying solely on the non-atomic pre-check.

idempotent_creation.note: POST /api/registry/entries had no idempotency concept: the name-only draft branch synthesized a fresh random strategy_id on every call, so a caller could not safely retry a dropped response without creating a second, divergent draft. An optional Idempotency-Key header now scopes creation through RegistryService.register_with_idempotency, backed by a new create_with_receipt on both storage backends (mirroring commit_metadata_cas's atomic reservation-then-commit pattern on Postgres, sharing one transaction with the entry insert). A replay under the same tenant/actor-scoped key returns the originally-created entry; the identity-generating factory is only invoked on a genuine first request. This is scoped to the generic entries route in this pass; register_strategy_spec/register_strategy_artifact/register_allocation_policy_artifact already have content-addressed idempotency via register_if_absent's composite-key replay match.

readiness_owner_dependency.note: services/registry/main.py registered /healthz//livez//readyz with no dependency check at all, so /readyz always returned 200/ready=true/dependencies={} regardless of whether the selected owner backend was actually reachable, including when backend selection silently resolved to the in-memory test double. main.py now registers a `registry_owner` dependency that performs a genuine short-lived Postgres connection probe (SELECT 1) on the durable backend, or explicitly reports `degraded`/`backend: memory` when the in-memory test double is selected, on every readiness check.
readiness_owner_dependency.remaining_gap: Not proven against a live Postgres outage/partition in this pass; the connection probe itself is genuine (fresh connect + SELECT 1, not a cached pool), but no test kills the database mid-run to observe the transition to error status.

auth_wiring_status.note: architecture-resumption-sa-sd.md §3.3 requires reusing services/runtime_auth_inbound.py validate_request_auth with strict mode across Registry mutation routes. The 2026-09-06 corrective pass wires _authenticate_registry_write into every mutating route in service.py (register_entry, register_strategy_spec, register_strategy_artifact, register_allocation_policy_artifact, every advance route, mutate_strategy_artifact_entry, update_deployment_summary) — not just the metadata-CAS route — and additionally rejects a signature-valid JWT missing subject/tenant/role/expiry claims via _require_verified_identity. docker-compose.yml and docker-compose.control.yml already set PANTHEON_REGISTRY_AUTH_MODE=strict and REGISTRY_STORE_BACKEND=postgres for the registry service. A follow-up gen-5 pass additionally scopes register_strategy_spec's replay-return path (and the cross-tenant aggregate reads named above) through _authorize_write/_can_read_entry, since authentication alone does not scope which tenant's data a verified caller may read back.
